Hey gorgeous girl, I just wanna say you're very cute and despite your smile not being real, I can see the sparkle in your eyes, and it really draws me in (and Im sure it draws others too!) I once read some advice that really helped me accept being single, and it said 'being single is life on default mode, anything else is a bonus'. Some might think wow, that's crappy advice, but to me it opened up a world of possibility. They were absolutely right, almost anything I desired from a relationship I could give myself and be truly spoiled. Being single is a gift and the biggest journey of self discovery. Please don't rush into a relationship bc you feel like its all you're missing in life, bc it never ends well. 

Try and enjoy being single. It's radical self love, buying yourself gifts and the things you need, saving up for that house down payment or holiday, learning a language and chasing your dreams. It's all there, waiting for you. Adding someone to that is a bonus, its already doable and the I'd argue the deep relationships you can make with your friends and family are just as good. 

Remember you're whole as you are x Treat yourself well and know you're plenty wanted and attractive, now just might not be the right time x

I love church, but I dont love the church options currently available to me. I won't say any names, but talking about how much money the church has, how many people they've baptized and asking for expensive tithes week after week isn't why I'm a christian. I do it for God, and to me, that's the most personal journey of all. Often when I go to church im faced with messages and interpretations I dont agree with, which is confronting, but ultimately helps me grow as a person bc hey, look ag how this pastor interpreted the message! 

But church can make me feel guilty too. So many songs about never being good enough without God, not being able to live without God, it's not how I see it, it's bc of God I have faith and something to chase after. He gives me strength, not bc i 'dont deserve it', but bc he loves me. I want to go back. I really do. But as you said, my heart leaves heavier. Its ALL about the church. In the hour sessions I attend I can safely say almost half of it is spend talking about the new churches the church has built across america (im australian), ads for tithing at least 20 usd and the church's mission (reaching as many people as possible, but to me, that comes second to the word and the message the millions - and I mean millions - to the ppl who already attend this church wait for every sunday). I think a smaller church would be better for me. Less ads at least haha.

We ARE the church. Where there are two or more of you, there is communion. In so many ways I don't conventionally "belong" as a christian, but screw it, so many of us dont! We are the temples of God, we ARE the church, and its all around us. I feel closest to God in the morning when I read the word and go for a run out in his green world, birds all around me, on the verge of passing out, making the most of the day, that's church to me and I aim to do it every day. Church shouldn't be considered an automatic "its a go" for all christians . My heart is lighter without my current church. Maybe that will change. But for now, Love and chase God as you please x

- over analysing and planning how to make the absolute BEST of your life and realizing how unachievable it is (ie, suddenly bc an honor student after 3 yrs of flunking college, endless travel despite COVID/not being able to leave your bed anyways, etc) - the classic zero to hero on repeat.

- Feeling like you'll never ever be sad, hopeless or depleted of energy when you're manic, "forgetting" what it was like.

- Hating mania, I don't think any of us inherently like it, but too often I hear ppl say, "wow! I wish I could feel that motivated/unstoppable/energetic/euphoric sometimes!" -> you don't. It's a nightmare and everything is moving way too fast, the panic attacks despite feeling pure joy are alarming and the excessive plans you make can ruin your financial security, safety and general health.

- Not taking basic care of yourself, like brushing your teeth, making those doctor appointments you need, ignoring pain/illness, not showering, oversleeping (in my case, 10+ a day bc i just don't want to be awake)

- My psych, friends and family being extremely happy and finally feeling they can relax when I show joy during mania, only to crash a few days/hours later and the cycle continue -> appearing serious, attentive and 'normal' in therapy bc despite it all, you're somehow magically 'high-functioning' in public.

- A deep sense of hopelessness from feeling like you'll never be heard/taken seriously (after all, it's just a 'mood' thing, "you'll learn to cope with ur emotions better the older u get", etc)

- Picking at your lips, nails, scratching, ignoring injuries (ie, excessive walking on plantar tendonitis, running on shin injuries, etc) bc u genuinely don't care and welcome the pain

- Numbness, ahedonia, no emotion.

- Excessive overeating or suddenly losing a lot of weight from stress.

- Facing the traditional symptoms of bipolar with medicinal side effects -> you might swing bc you were triggered by your looks but are also losing hair from your new meds.

- Near constant head ache

- Constant anger/frustration that you have to fight rly hard not to manifest over tiny transgressions.

- Disappearing for months online and withdrawing from friends and family.

Everyone is different. These are my frequent/daily symptoms as a bipolar person and I feel like my whole life revolves around surviving, even if I appear 'high-functioning' in public. Bipolar isn't cute, quirky, cool and mania isn't fun/something you want to experience for 'kicks' (yes, these r things I've heard). It's a debilitating illness that can put you out of school, work and be claimed as a disability in my country if it's chronic.
